_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Inside Decoded, 48K views, 2 weeks old; AI/altered-content label). Frames every 0.5 s for the first 4 s then every 5-8 s; no sound probe. Shots approximate. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a glossy black folding phone lying open on a dark studio floor with a faint grid, a bright light streak across its screen
hook.firstLine: Foldable phones have been around for years

shots.picture: glossy folding phone on a dark grid floor, slow push-in until it fills the frame; a tiny image-credit pill top-right
a bluer new phone head-on, a thin leader line to a name tag
close on the bright screen surface
cross-section slab of screen layers seen edge-on
the layered panel bent into a tight U, an 'illustrative' pill
close on a hinge mechanism, the panel curling around it
exploded view: dozens of hinge parts floating in rows
close on the hinge's curved channel
stacked layers of the panel separating upward from the phone
macro texture of tiny bumps on the screen surface
the phone open on the grid, a light sweeping over the fold line
hinge with a support-bar label, then the closed phone on the grid

lines.gist: folding phones have existed for years and you can still see the crease
the new one hides it; within hours people looked for it
why screens crease: layers stretch when folded tight
the hinge curls the screen into a teardrop and has over a hundred parts
a wider curve and support under the panel mean less stretch
tiny bumps still form; with time it may get worse
so the crease is still there, just hard to see

ending.lastFrame: the phone on the dark grid floor, as at the start

whyItWorks: a premium product-render look: glossy object, dark grid floor, one moving light streak
the hidden part is shown by cutaways and exploded views, never by a diagram on a card
the title states a surprising truth the viewer can check on their own phone
small credit pills (image source, illustrative) keep it trustworthy without clutter
